claims.event: Governor of Yingchuan for eight years, praised by edict for transforming the people and granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes, then summoned as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
Younger brother of the Xiongnu chanyu, sent to attend the Han court in the fifth month.
Governor of Henan from Donghai called the Butcher Lord for his cruelty; denounced by Yi, he was convicted of impiety and executed, as his mother had foretold.
Assistant prefect of Henan and former fellow clerk of Yan Yannian who, fearing him, memorialized ten charges against him and then took poison.
Violent chanyu deserted by the left territory nobles; defeated by Huhanye’s forces and rebuffed by his brother the Right Worthy King, he killed himself.
Eastern Xiongnu king raided by the Wuhuan who, fearing the chanyu, joined Wuchanmu in installing Ji Houyu as Chanyu Huhanye.
Joined the Guxi King and the left territory nobles in installing Ji Houyu as Chanyu Huhanye.
Installed as Chanyu Huhanye by the eastern nobles, he drove Woyu Jodi to suicide, then was defeated by Chanyu Tujue’s surprise attack.
Younger brother of Woyu Jodi who refused him aid, co-installed Chanyu Tujue, and was later killed with his son by Tujue on false charges.
Left Grand Commandant who fled to the Right Worthy King, helped install Chanyu Tujue, and was sent against Wujie.
Elder brother of Huhanye, found living among the commoners and installed as Left Guli King.
Rizhu King installed as Chanyu Tujue by Dulongqi and the Right Worthy King; he routed Huhanye and fought the rival chanyus Chelí and Wujie.
Eldest son of Chanyu Tujue, made Left Guli King.
Younger son of Chanyu Tujue, made Right Guli King.
Xiongnu noble whose elder brother, the Right Aojian King, was sent east by Tujue against Huhanye.
Sent east by Tujue against Huhanye, he proclaimed himself Chanyu Chelí and was backed by Wujie and Hujie until Tujue defeated him.
Commandant sent east by Tujue who proclaimed himself Chanyu Wujie, was defeated by Dulongqi, and gave up the title to support Chelí.
Western king who slandered the Right Worthy King, then fearing Tujue proclaimed himself Chanyu Hujie before yielding the title to Chelí.
Joined the Hujie King in slandering the Right Worthy King and was killed by Tujue when the charge proved false.

claims.event: As censor-in-chief he advised against exploiting the Xiongnu civil war; after clashing with Han Yanshou and slighting Chancellor Bing Ji he was demoted to Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
Jin commander cited by Xiao Wangzhi for turning back from Qi on hearing of the Qi ruler’s death.
Replaced Xiao Wangzhi as Left Governor of Feng; after their mutual investigations he was convicted of cunning impiety and executed, mourned by thousands at Weicheng.
General of Chariots and Cavalry whose death is recorded in the first year entry.
General who in the fifth month became Grand Marshal and Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
Aged chancellor esteemed by the emperor, whose slighting by Xiao Wangzhi led to Xiao’s demotion; he died as Marquis Ding of Boyang.
Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent promoted to Censor-in-Chief when Xiao Wangzhi was demoted.
As Chanyu Huhanye he sent his brother west against Tujue, defeated Tujue, received Chelí’s submission and beheaded the restored Wujie chanyu.
Chanyu Tujue, who attacked Huhanye with sixty thousand horse, was defeated and killed himself.
After Tujue’s suicide he fled to Han with Tujue’s son Gumoloutou.
Younger son of Tujue and Right Guli King who fled to Han with Dulongqi.
As Chanyu Chelí he submitted in the east to Chanyu Huhanye.
Huhanye’s Left Grand General who surrendered to Han with his father and was enfeoffed Marquis of Xincheng.
Surrendered to Han with his son Wuliju and tens of thousands of followers and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yiyang.
Han general whose son reinstalled the Wujie commandant as chanyu.
Reinstalled as chanyu by Li Ling’s son and captured and beheaded by Huhanye.
Cousin of Tujue who set himself up in the west as Chanyu Runzhen.
Elder brother of Huhanye who as Left Worthy King set himself up in the east as Chanyu Zhizhi Gudu-hou.
Superintendent of the imperial household and Marquis of Pingtong whose quarrel with Dai Changle led to both being dismissed as commoners.
Grand Coachman who accused Yang Yun of seditious talk and was himself dismissed as a commoner.
Palace gentleman who asked Yang Yun whether Han Yanshou would survive his lawsuit.
Scholar whose sayings on overcast skies without rain Yang Yun quoted to Dai Changle.
Minister of Justice who found Yang Yun guilty of resentment, evil words and great impiety.

Marquis of Leling and palace attendant, a maternal relative of the emperor whom Huang Ba improperly recommended as Grand Marshal.
Governor of Xihe appointed Censor-in-Chief in the sixth month.
Prince of Guangling who had a witch curse the emperor, poisoned witnesses when discovered, and killed himself; posthumously Prince Li.
Witch employed by Liu Xu to curse the emperor, later poisoned to silence her.
Proposed buying grain near the capital and founding Ever-Normal Granaries, for which he was made Marquis within the Passes.
Dismissed from rank, he answered Sun Huizong’s rebuke with a defiant letter and was executed at the waist after Wang Cheng’s accusation.
Governor of Anding who warned Yang Yun to live humbly; dismissed when Yang’s reply was found.
Marquis of Anping, nephew of Yang Yun, who urged him that he would be employed again and was dismissed as a commoner in his fall.
Cited by Tan as a hard-working official executed for his case.
Groom who blamed Yang Yun for the solar eclipse in a memorial.
Guard of the Weiyang Palace dismissed as a close friend of Yang Yun.

Appointed Commandant of Huaiyang to set Prince Xian an example, having once yielded his rank to his elder brother.

Right Wise King and son of Huhanye, sent to attend the Han court.

Right Grand General and son of Zhizhi, sent to attend the Han court.
Marquis Jing of Lecheng, whose death is recorded in the second month.
Former emperor whose temple caught fire.

Palace general sent with medicine to treat the Mad King.
The Fat King of Wusun, father of Wujiutu.

Colonel of the Guard sent with troops against the rebellion in Zhuya Commandery.
Dismissed because of old age and illness.

Imperial son established as Prince of Dongping in the ninth month.
Marquis Zhuangwu of Yingping, retired for age but still consulted on frontier strategy, whose death is recorded this year.
Chanyu Huhanye, who came to Wuyuan Pass, attended court as a vassal not named, received lavish gifts and was escorted home.
Tutor of the Heir Apparent who argued the chanyu be received as a non-subject ranked above the feudal kings.
Eastern Han historian whose discussion criticizes Xiao Wangzhi’s proposal as contrary to ritual.
Commandant of Cavalry sent to welcome the chanyu and later to escort him out through Jilu Pass.
Commandant of the Changle Guard and Marquis of Gaochang, who escorted the chanyu home and stayed to guard him.
